assertion: US traffic deaths fell in the first half of this year to the lowest rate since 2014, the government said on Tuesday.
independent_value: Reuters copies report NHTSA H1 2026 rate 1.02 per 100M VMT. NHTSA release not opened; a secondary summary calls 1.02 the second-lowest half-year rate on record. Early estimate/projection.
searched: US traffic deaths first half 2026 NHTSA lowest rate since 2014

assertion: traffic deaths dropped 2.5% to 16,750 in the first half of the year. It was the lowest number since 2015 and down from 17,175 in the same period last year.
independent_value: 16,750 vs 17,175 = -2.47%. Annual FARS 2014 32,744, 2015 35,484. NHTSA's earlier H1 2025 estimate was 17,140 (revised). Early estimate; NSC (different definition) counts 18,460, -2%.

sources.title: NSC first half 2026 via Carrier Management

assertion: This year is on pace to be the fifth straight year of declines.
independent_value: FARS 2021 43,230 > 2022 42,721 > 2023 41,025 > 2024 39,254; NHTSA says 2025 lowest since 2019; 2026 H1 -2.5%. Fifth straight is a projection; Q2 fell only 0.2%.

assertion: US traffic deaths jumped 10.8% in 2021 to 43,230, the most in a single year since 2005.
independent_value: 2005 FARS about 43,510 (public NHTSA figure), so 2021 highest since 2005.

assertion: Full-year traffic deaths for 2025 fell to the lowest number since 2019 and the fatality rate fell to 1.10 fatalities per 100 million vehicle miles traveled, the second-lowest yearly figure in US history, NHTSA said.
independent_value: NHTSA-sourced coverage reports 2025 rate 1.10, second-lowest ever. FARS 2024 39,254 vs 2019 36,355 consistent. 2025 not in warehouse.

assertion: Deaths fell 5% in the first three months of 2026 but just 0.2% in the second three months.
independent_value: NHTSA Q1 early estimate 7,770, -4.3% (article's 5% plausibly a revision). Q2 -0.2% only in Reuters.

assertion: One area of concern remains bicyclist deaths, which rose 4% to 1,148 last year. In 2023, bicyclist deaths hit their highest figure in more than four decades.
why_not: The only place the 4% and 1,148 appear is the Reuters article itself; that passage is the claim, not corroboration.
why_no_page: Opened NHTSA crashstats publication 813833 (Q1 2026 early estimate), searched all pages for bicyclist/1,148: no match. Searches for the 2025 bicyclist count found no page carrying it. Warehouse FARS ends 2024 with no bicyclist breakdown.
reason: No accessible source carries the 2025 bicyclist figure.

assertion: A 2023 NHTSA study found crashes directly cost taxpayers $30 billion, and society as a whole $340 billion. When quality-of-life valuations were included, the total cost to society ran to $1.37 trillion.
independent_value: Matches NHTSA's published 2023 study of 2019 crash costs; not re-opened.
searched: NHTSA economic and societal cost of motor vehicle crashes 2019 $340 billion $1.37 trillion

assertion: As US roads became less crowded during the pandemic, some motorists perceived police as less likely to issue tickets, experts said, resulting in riskier driving.
independent_value: Widely cited hypothesis attributed to unnamed experts; hedged; not causally established.
